questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend re-running the pre-launch checklist live, the morning of launch, rather than trusting it from an earlier review?
options: To confirm it's still true right now, not based on how things looked when it was last checked
Because the checklist from Lesson 26 is no longer relevant by launch day
Live re-checks are purely a formality with no practical purpose
The checklist only needs to be run once, at any point before launch
questions.explain: Conditions can change between when a checklist was last confirmed and the actual launch morning -- re-running it live confirms current reality, not a memory of it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a contract should be verified on the block explorer before the launch is announced publicly?
options: A live but unverified contract invites exactly the wrong kind of attention and looks unfinished at the worst possible moment
Verification is only necessary after a launch has already been publicly announced
Block explorers cannot verify a contract once it has been deployed
Announcing before verification has no practical downside
questions.explain: Confirming source matches bytecode before announcing avoids drawing attention to a contract that looks unaccountable or unfinished.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend resisting the urge to raise the deposit cap in the first hours after launch, even if nothing has gone wrong?
options: Nothing going wrong in the first hour isn't sufficient evidence yet -- real evidence takes longer to gather than early excitement does
Caps should never be raised under any circumstances, ever
Raising the cap early is always safe as long as the audit passed
The cap can only be raised by the original contract deployer personally
questions.explain: This reinforces Lesson 28's point: raising a cap needs real evidence of clean usage over time, not the absence of problems in the first hour.

questions.q: According to the 'if something does go wrong' runbook in this lesson, what should happen first?
options: Confirm the incident is real, before pausing, communicating, investigating, or running a postmortem
Immediately post a public postmortem before confirming any facts
Redeploy the contract from scratch without investigating
Wait 48 hours before taking any action at all
questions.explain: The runbook sequence starts with confirming the incident is real (Chapter 5, Lesson 24) before any further action is taken.

questions.q: What course does this lesson name as the next and final course in the Blockchain Engineer path?
options: Blockchain Engineering Capstones
Blockchain Development
A repeat of this same course from Lesson 1
There is no further course in the path
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names Blockchain Engineering Capstones as the final course, where everything from this course and earlier ones comes together in end-to-end projects.
